teaser: A token behaviour policy as a 132-line hook: the user sees what each session reads, caches and costs; a prompt cannot do it.
core_idea: Tokens deserve their own small agent behaviour policy, observe mode first: a Claude Code hook that reads only the new lines of the session transcript, counts each response once, prices it by model and shows the user a box of reads, cache share, writes, context and cost; asked through a prompt, the model correctly said it could not see its usage, while the hook gave exact figures one turn behind in about a millisecond; building it exposed double counting in our own session report and showed the transcript carries the system prompt and tool definitions; caching was 99% of this session's input, and the brief is a site, tokens.hook.sgit.ai, that treats one small hook as mission-critical code.
